chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Isma'il ibn Mansur, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Humran, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever marries a woman when the moon is in the Scorpion (constellation), he will not see the good (or happiness).'

key_terms.الْحُسْنَى: The good, happiness, or prosperity; often used to denote the positive outcome of an action.
key_terms.الْعَقْرَبِ: The Scorpion (constellation), referring to a specific lunar mansion or astrological sign.
key_terms.تَزَوَّجَ: He married; the act of entering into a marriage contract.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of marrying during the lunar phase of Al-Aqrab according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links marital harmony to the lunar mansion of Al-Aqrab, reflecting the Shia tradition of *ilm al-nujum* (astral influence) on human affairs. The term 'al-husna' implies a lack of enduring bliss or prosperity, suggesting that while not necessarily a permanent curse, such timing may hinder the spiritual and emotional depth of the union. This ruling is often contextualized within the broader Shia understanding of how celestial configurations can subtly affect worldly outcomes, distinct from divine decree.
